result.document_summary: A Morgan Lewis LawFlash (Aug. 21, 2026) describing new state and local algorithmic rent-pricing laws and the follow-on litigation they have spawned, with a table summarizing ordinances in several cities.
result.notes: Secondary law-firm summary. Records are limited to in-scope manifest jurisdictions (San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley, Santa Ana, Jersey City, Hoboken); other cities (Seattle, Philadelphia, Providence, Minneapolis, Portland, Spokane, Rockville, King County) were skipped as outside the allowed jurisdiction list. The page gives only month-level effective dates for most ordinances, so those are recorded at YYYY-MM precision. It does not set out coverage or exemptions, so coverage is left empty. The Hoboken citation is as given on the page ("ch. 158-2") and may be imprecise. Berkeley's ordinance is noted as previously challenged in RealPage v. City of Berkeley, voluntarily dismissed with prejudice Jan. 14, 2026; it is recorded as enacted.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy. Each month of use per affected unit may be a separate violation; tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each unit-month may be a separate violation
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance prohibits landlords from using qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords using qualifying algorithmic devices in San Francisco; the page does not state further coverage conditions.

rules.title: San Diego prohibition on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: San Diego bars use of algorithmic devices relying on competitor data to set rents and authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Each month and each affected rental property may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each month and property may be a separate violation
rules.quoted_span: San Diego similarly authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_text: Landlords using algorithmic rent-setting devices in San Diego; the page does not state further coverage conditions.

rules.title: Berkeley prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Berkeley prohibits coordinated rent-pricing algorithms, with recurring unit/month violations and private remedies. The city's ordinance was previously challenged in RealPage, Inc. v. City of Berkeley, which was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on Jan. 14, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms; recurring unit/month violations and private remedies
rules.coverage_text: Landlords using coordinated pricing algorithms in Berkeley; the page does not state further coverage conditions.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing. Tenants may bring private claims for up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords engaging in automated rent price-fixing in Santa Ana; the page does not state further coverage conditions.

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ordinance is enforceable both publicly and privately, with fines of up to $2,000 per day.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords using algorithmic rent coordination services in Jersey City; the page does not state further coverage conditions.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on software used to coordinate rents
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents in Hoboken; the page does not state further coverage conditions.
